verdicts.claim: Thinking toggle via enable_thinking, ON by default; generation prompt '<_bot><think>\n' or '<_bot></think>'
verdicts.correction: chat_template.jinja line 109 matches. Earlier assistant turns (before the last user message) are rendered with '</think>' only, so reasoning is dropped from history. In HF discussion #5, Prophet000 (isOrgMember true) confirms that non-thinking mode is weaker.

verdicts.claim: Tool calling format: <tool_call>{name}<param_key>..</param_key><param_value>..</param_value></tool_call>; tools as JSON in <tools>; results via <_observation><tool_response>; <tool_call>/<tool_response> special, <param_key>/<param_value> not
verdicts.correction: Template lines 30-45 and 80-103 match, and the tokenizer_config special tokens (ids 11-14) match. <_observation> is not among the added special tokens either. Added risk (inferred): line 86-87 calls tc.arguments.items(), so the template breaks when a client sends arguments as a JSON string, which is the OpenAI default, unless the runtime turns them into an object first. That needs checking in the llama.cpp smoke test.

verdicts.claim: HF discussion #15: the responder's diagnosis, and that temperature 0 for tool turns is 'community advice, not vendor guidance'
verdicts.correction: The responder, xiongji ('bear'), has isOrgMember true and belongs only to the XingChen-AGI org, so this is vendor-staff guidance. It is still informal and conflicts with the card's 0.8 for coding/agent work. The numbers are confirmed: 4446 vs 9937 tokens, max_tokens 2048 truncated 5/5 and 8192 succeeded 5/5, and at temperature 1.0 the model sometimes drops the <tool_call> wrapper or emits bare JSON. The original user's reply (2026-11-05) says it still fails with 65536 output tokens on the Pi harness. The thread is still open.

verdicts.correction: Qwen's own card (lastModified 2026-11-07) gives Qwen3.6-35B-A3B SWE-bench Verified 73.4, not 76.0, and 51.5 is Qwen's Terminal-Bench 2.0 score (Terminus-2, temp 1.0, 5 runs), which Xing relabels as TB 2.1. Xing's Gemma4-26B-A4B figures also disagree with Qwen's card: SWE-V 53.0 vs 17.4, SWE-Multi 51.0 vs 17.3, TB 30.0 vs 34.2. So the head-to-head table mixes benchmark versions and sources.

verdicts.claim: KV math: MLA 46,080 B/token BF16 (40 layers), q8_0 24,480 B/token; vLLM pool negative
verdicts.correction: Source-backed arithmetic: (512+64) x 2 x 40 = 46,080, and 576 x 34/32 x 40 = 24,480. 14.65 - 30.89 - 1.2 = -17.44 GiB. With the MTP layer loaded (41 layers) it becomes 47,232 B/token f16.

summary: I found nothing invented. Vendor identity (TeleAI/China Telecom, unverified orgs), dates, config, context, license, the thinking toggle, the tool format, every checkpoint size and the llama.cpp and vLLM status all match live primary sources. Three corrections. (1) The vendor's head-to-head table is unreliable. Qwen's own card gives Qwen3.6-35B-A3B SWE-bench Verified 73.4, not 76.0. The 51.5 is Qwen's Terminal-Bench 2.0 score, relabeled as 2.1. The Gemma4-26B figures also disagree with Qwen's card. All Xing scores are self-reported, and no independent benchmark exists. (2) In HF discussion #15, the person advising temperature 0 and max_tokens of at least 8192 is a XingChen-AGI org member (xiongji), so this is informal vendor-staff advice, not community advice. The original user still reports failures at 65k output, and the thread is open. (3) The official GGUF weights, including iq2_M-slim (uploaded 2026-10-23), also predate the 2026-11-05 llama.cpp merge, not just the Venastine ones. Their header keys match b12407 names, but a full load is unverified. Added risk (inferred): the template calls tc.arguments.items(), so string-encoded tool arguments may break rendering. Include this in the OpenCode smoke test. Work files are in $SCRATCH/xingchk/.
